1  TRIBUNAL RAIBAG & ETC.
 THIS MFA, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE  COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  MFA No. 20413 of 2011  JUDGMENT Respondent No.1-insured is impugning the judgment and award dated 14.10.2010 passed in M.V.C.
No. 2369/2005 by the MACT, Raibag (hereinafter referred to as the Tribunal), allowing the claim petition awarding compensation of Rs.87,500/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation and directing respondent No.1 to deposit the amount within 30 days while dismissing the claim petition against the respondent no.2-insurer.
Parties shall be referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.
2.
Brief facts of the case are that the claimant filed the claim petition u/S 166 of the M.V. Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.

It is stated that on 22.06.2005 he was traveling in the tempo trax bearing reg. no. KA-23/M-3576 which met with an accident due to the rash and negligent driving by its driver and it hit to a telephone pole.
The claimant sustained injuries, was admitted to the hospital and had spent huge amount for his treatment.
Therefore, he claimed compensation from respondent Nos.1 and 2 being the insured and insurer of the offending vehicle.

The respondent No.1-owner of the offending vehicle filed objection statement denying the contention of the claimant, however, he contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was having driving licence to drive the same and the vehicle in question was insured with respondent No.2 and therefore it was respondent No.2 who is liable to pay compensation.
Respondent No.2-insurer of the offending vehicle filed objection statement denying the contentions taken by the claimant and its liability to pay compensation.
It is denied that the tempo trax in question was insured with the respondent and submitted that even if it is insured, its liability will be subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

3. On the basis of these pleadings, the following issues were came to be framed:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent or due to actionable negligence of the driver of the tempo trax bearing reg. no.
KA-23/M-3576 as alleged?
2. Whether petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in the said accident?

Pundalik S/O Bhimappa Akale vs Krishna S/O Muttappa Chinchalli on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93046244/
2 3.
Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, for what amount and from whom?
4. What order or award?
The claimant examined PWs.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.P.1 to 26 in support of his contention.
The respondents examined RWs.1 and 2 in support of their contention and got marked Exs.R.1 to R14 in support of their contention.

The Tribunal after taking into consideration all these materials on record awarded compensation of Rs.87,500/- with interest at 6% p.a. to be paid by the respondent No.1 and dismissed the claim petition against respondent No.2.
Being aggrieved by the same, the insured is before this Court.

4. Heard Sri Shivaraj S. Ballolli, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri S.S. Joshi, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
5.

Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the vehicle in question was insured with respondent No.2 and the Insurance Policy is marked as Ex.R.1, which is a comprehensive policy covering the risk of the inmates of the vehicle.
Extra premium of Rs.450/- was paid which covers the risk of 9 (nine) unnamed inmates / passengers.
Under such circumstances, respondent No.2 could not have avoided the liability.
He placed reliance on the decision of the Division Bench of this Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Kalawati1 in support of his contention.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Kalawati1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, prays for allowing the appeal saddling liability on the insurer.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurer opposing the appeal submitted that even though the vehicle was insured, the same was subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
As per the insurance policy it covers the risk of the inmates but not when it is for hire or reward.
When such a specific condition was violated, the compensation is to be paid by the insured himself.

7. Learned counsel further submitted that in the case of Kalawathi (supra), there was no evidence to show that the vehicle in question was plied for hire or reward, but in the present case there is evidence available on record and therefore the insurer cannot be saddled with liability.
The Tribunal rightly exonerated the insurer from liability which do not call for any interference.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.
Perused the material on record including the trial Court records.

9. In view of the contentions raised by the appellant, the point that arises for consideration is:
Whether the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal calls for interference by this Court?
10.

My answer to the above point is in the affirmative for the following:
Pundalik S/O Bhimappa Akale vs Krishna S/O Muttappa Chinchalli on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93046244/
3 REASONS 11.

entities.text: Bhimappa Akale vs Krishna S/O Muttappa Chinchalli
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is the specific contention of the appellant that he was traveling in the tempo trax bearing reg.
no. KA-23/M-3576 when it met with an accident and he sustained injuries.

The Tribunal awarded compensation in favour of the claimant againt respondent No.1 exonerating the respondent No.2 on the ground that use of the vehicle was for hire or reward in violation of the terms and conditions of the policy-Ex.R.1.
12.
Ex.R.1 is the copy of the policy which is admittedly a comprehensive policy.

As rightly pointed out by the learned counsel for the appellant, the risk of 9 (nine) unnamed inmates/ passengers at Rs.1 lakh per person was covered by collecting extra premium of Rs.450/- with compulsorily coverage of owner and driver at Rs.2 lakhs.

The tribunal awarded the compensation only at Rs.
87,500/-, which is within the limitation covered under the policy.
Of course, the limitation to the use is mentioned that the policy covered for use of vehicle for any purpose other than hire and reward.

13. The Division Bench of this Court in Kalawathi (supra), considering the similar situation at paragraph no.4 has held as under:
"4. That apart we do not find any rationale for the insurer as a 'State' to discriminate between the paid inmate and the gratuitous inmate when the vehicle is covered with comprehensive policy.

If the vehicle is a private vehicle plyed on hire, the owner may be liable for the penal and fiscal consequences under the Motor Vehicle Act for payment of penalty and taxes applicable to the commercial vehicles.
But from the stand-point of the insurer, it makes no difference whether the inmate is a paid passenger or gratuitous passenger.
When the policy issued is a comprehensive policy covering risk of the inmates of a private vehicle, the insurer cannot avoid liability on the ground that the inmate is a paid passenger.

In that view, we hold that the terms in the policy, which discriminates the liability of the insurer for the paid inmate and gratuitous inmate is discriminatory and illegal."
14.

Of course, on facts of the case, it is held there is no express averments made that the jeep in question was taken on hire for the purpose of journey and even the evidence of PW1 in the said aspect does not disclose that the jeep was hired for their journey.

But in the present case evidence of PW1 discloses that he boarded the tempo trax in the middle and he was not knowing either the driver or the owner, which could reasonably be concluded that he was carried for hire and reward.

But the Division Bench of this Court made it clear that the insurer cannot differentiate between the inmates as paid passengers or gratuitous passenger when the risk of inmates is comprehensively covered by collecting extra premium.
Avoiding liability by the insurer on the ground that the inmate is a gratuitous passenger/ inmate is already held to be discriminatory and illegal.
Therefore, the decision referred to above aptly applies to the facts of the case.
Therefore, the insurer could not have made such a differentiation and could not have avoided its liability to pay compensation.
15. Hence, I am of the opinion that the impugned judgment and award saddling liability on respondent No.1-insured is liable to be set aside.

It is held that both the insured and insurer are Pundalik S/O Bhimappa Akale vs Krishna S/O Muttappa Chinchalli on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93046244/
4 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the claimant.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following order.
ORDER Appeal is allowed with costs.

Impugned judgment and award dated 14.10.2010 passed in M.V.C. No. 2369/2005 by the MACT,
Raibag, is modified to the extent that both the insurer and insured are liable to pay the compensation jointly and severally.

Respondent No.2-insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with up to date interest,
within two months from the date of the award.
Draw decree accordingly.
Amount in deposit made by the appellant shall be refunded on due identification.
Send back the trial Court records along with copy of the judgment and award.
